subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Threatened, Inevitable, Incomplete, Missed and Septic Abortion

steps.tx: Bleeding in early pregnancy with a closed cervix and living fetus is **threatened abortion**. Most such pregnancies continue normally after the bleeding settles. Ultrasound confirming cardiac activity guides reassurance and follow up. About half of women with bleeding and a closed cervix go on to deliver a live baby at term.
steps.say: Threatened abortion bleeds with a closed cervix and most pregnancies continue normally.

steps.tx: An abortion that cannot be stopped because the cervix has opened is **inevitable abortion**. Membranes may bulge through the cervix on examination. Management supports completion with evacuation when needed. Bulging membranes through an open cervix cannot be pushed back, and expectant care ends in delivery within days.
steps.say: Inevitable abortion cannot be stopped once the cervix has opened.

steps.tx: Partial passage of products leaving tissue inside the uterus is **incomplete abortion**. Bleeding can be heavy because retained tissue prevents uterine contraction. Evacuation by suction or medical method completes the process. A uterus larger than expected with a rapid pulse suggests blood loss beyond what is seen externally.
steps.say: Incomplete abortion retains tissue that prevents contraction and causes heavy bleeding.

steps.tx: Fetal death without expulsion, often found on routine scan, is **missed abortion**. The uterus fails to grow and pregnancy symptoms fade. Expectant, medical and surgical options are all offered by gestation and preference. A crown rump length over 7 millimetres with no heartbeat, or a sac over 25 millimetres with no embryo, confirms the diagnosis.
steps.say: Missed abortion is fetal death without expulsion, found on routine scanning.

steps.tx: Infected retained products causing fever, pain and offensive discharge define **septic abortion**. It follows unsafe abortion practices and can progress to septic shock. Resuscitation, antibiotics and urgent evacuation save lives. Broad spectrum antibiotics start before evacuation, and group A streptococcus is the organism most feared for rapid collapse.
steps.say: Septic abortion infects retained products and can progress to septic shock.

steps.tx: Medical abortion using mifepristone followed by misoprostol is standard to nine weeks and beyond in many protocols, termed **medical termination**. Success exceeds ninety five percent in early gestation. Surgical backup covers the small failure group. Mifepristone 200 milligrams is followed 24 to 48 hours later by misoprostol 800 micrograms, usually vaginally or sublingually.
steps.say: Medical termination with mifepristone and misoprostol succeeds in over ninety five percent early.

steps.tx: Rh negative women need anti-D after abortion to prevent **isoimmunisation**. Even early sensitisation can affect future pregnancies. Guidelines vary by gestation and method, so local protocol is followed. Anti-D 250 international units covers most first trimester events, with larger doses after later gestations.
steps.say: Anti-D after abortion prevents isoimmunisation in Rh negative women.

steps.tx: Complete passage of all products with settling bleeding is **complete abortion**. Ultrasound showing an empty uterus confirms it. No evacuation is needed and routine follow up suffices. Bleeding that soaks a pad an hour for two hours after a presumed complete abortion means retained tissue until proved otherwise.
steps.say: Complete abortion passes everything with settling bleeding and needs no evacuation.

steps.tx: Bleeding after twelve weeks with pain suggests placental causes rather than abortion, a matter of **differential diagnosis**. Cervical causes, ectopic pregnancy and molar disease also present with early bleeding. Ultrasound location and viability sort most cases quickly. A subchorionic haematoma on scan explains many such bleeds and usually resolves without treatment.
steps.say: Early bleeding differentials include ectopic and molar disease, sorted quickly by ultrasound.
